h1: Expired Registration & Inspection Sticker Tickets in El Paso
intro: An expired registration or inspection ticket in El Paso is usually the easiest citation on your windshield to make go away — if it's handled right. For a flat fee from $59, attorney Robert Navar works to have it dismissed and keeps a paperwork mistake from becoming a conviction.
summary: An expired registration ticket in El Paso is a Class C misdemeanor, but Texas law generally lets the court dismiss it if you register the vehicle within 20 working days of the citation and pay a small administrative fee (about $20).

Since 2025, Texas no longer requires a safety inspection for most non-commercial vehicles — the old inspection sticker is gone and a $7.50 inspection program replacement fee is collected with your registration instead. Older "expired inspection" tickets are often dismissable.
Paying the ticket instead of fixing it puts a conviction on your record and the court costs often exceed the fine. We handle the appearance so you never go to court.
Flat fees: $59 in El Paso Municipal Court, $69 in Justice of the Peace, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts. Hire online in two minutes.

sections.heading: Why an Expired Registration Ticket in El Paso Is Worth Fighting
paragraphs: Expired registration is the citation El Paso officers write most often as an add-on. You get pulled over on Montana Avenue or Mesa Street for something else, the officer runs the plate, and the sticker that lapsed two months ago becomes a second ticket. Many people assume it's a formality and just pay it. In Texas, paying is a guilty plea: the conviction goes on your record, and with court costs the total in El Paso is typically $100–$200 for a sticker you were going to renew anyway.

The frustrating part is that the law is built to let you out of this ticket. Texas Transportation Code 502.407 generally allows a judge to dismiss an expired-registration charge when the driver shows the vehicle was registered within 20 working days of the citation and pays an administrative fee of about $20. Courts in El Paso County apply this every day — but only if someone asks, with the right proof, before the case is treated as a default plea. That is the job our office does for you.
If the registration ticket came with a no-insurance or speeding citation from the same stop, we handle all of them together, and each extra citation is a discounted add-on on the checkout page.

sections.heading: Two Steps, One Sticker — and the 2025 Change to Texas Inspections
paragraphs: For years Texas ran the "Two Steps, One Sticker" program: you passed a safety inspection first, then renewed your registration, and a single windshield sticker covered both. That is why so many older tickets read "expired inspection" or "no inspection certificate."

Starting in 2025, Texas ended the annual safety inspection requirement for most non-commercial vehicles. In its place, the state collects an inspection program replacement fee of $7.50 as part of registration. (El Paso County is not one of the counties that still requires an emissions test, and commercial vehicles continue to have their own inspection rules.) The practical effect for drivers: there is no longer a separate inspection step for a personal car or pickup — you simply keep your registration current.

This matters for your ticket. If you were cited for an expired or missing inspection on a personal vehicle, the requirement the ticket is based on may no longer apply in the same way, and prosecutors in El Paso have been receptive to dismissing those cases. If you were cited for expired registration, the fix is the same as it always was: renew, bring the receipt, and let us ask the court for the statutory dismissal. Our ticket dismissal page explains what a dismissal means for your record.

paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance with the court the same business day, which stops any failure-to-appear problem and routes the court's notices to our office. Then we tell you exactly what to do on your end: renew the registration (online through the Texas DMV, at an El Paso County Tax Office location, or at a participating grocery store) and send us a photo of the receipt and the new sticker.

With that proof in hand, we present the case to the prosecutor and ask for the dismissal the statute allows. Where the 20-working-day window has already passed, we still have options: deferred disposition under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45.051, which ends in a dismissal with no conviction, or a negotiated outcome that keeps the violation off your record.

sections.heading: Fort Bliss, Out-of-State and Mexican Plates
paragraphs: El Paso's registration tickets have a local twist. Thousands of soldiers at Fort Bliss drive cars registered in Georgia, Kentucky or wherever they last served, and Texas does not require active-duty military to switch to Texas registration as long as the home-state registration is valid. An officer who sees an unfamiliar sticker may still write the ticket. If your out-of-state registration was current, we bring the proof and your military orders to the prosecutor, and these cases are routinely dismissed.

Civilians who move here for work face a different rule: Texas generally expects new residents to register within 30 days, and the first "welcome to Texas" ticket often arrives before the paperwork is done. Chihuahua plates on a car driven by an El Paso resident raise their own questions about where the vehicle is actually kept. Each situation has a defense, and the answer depends on the documents you can show. Not sure where your ticket was filed, or whether a missed date turned into a warrant? Use the free ticket and warrant lookup.

sections.heading: Which El Paso Court Has Your Registration Ticket
paragraphs: El Paso Police citations go to El Paso Municipal Court on Overland Avenue, where our flat fee is $59. Tickets from the Sheriff's Office, a DPS trooper on I-10 or a constable go to a Justice of the Peace precinct. Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony each run their own municipal courts; our fee in those courts is $69. The approach is the same everywhere: prove the fix, ask for the dismissal, and keep you out of the courtroom.

Check the appearance date printed on your citation, don't pay it, and don't miss it. If the date already passed, there may be a warrant and a separate failure-to-appear charge; our warrant recall page explains how we lift those, usually within a day or two. Se habla español. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case.

faqs.q: Can an expired registration ticket be dismissed in El Paso?
faqs.a: Generally, yes. Texas Transportation Code 502.407 lets the court dismiss the charge when you register the vehicle within 20 working days of the citation and pay an administrative fee of about $20. If you missed that window, we ask for deferred disposition or another outcome that avoids a conviction.

faqs.q: Do I still need a vehicle inspection in Texas?
faqs.a: For most non-commercial vehicles, no. Beginning in 2025 Texas ended the annual safety inspection and instead collects a $7.50 inspection program replacement fee with your registration. Commercial vehicles have separate rules, and a handful of larger counties still require emissions testing — El Paso County is not one of them.

faqs.q: What happens if I just pay the registration ticket?
faqs.a: Paying is a guilty plea. The conviction goes on your record, you pay the fine plus court costs, and you still have to renew the registration. Hiring us costs $59–$69 and in most cases ends with no conviction at all.

faqs.q: I'm stationed at Fort Bliss with out-of-state plates. Was the ticket valid?
faqs.a: Often not. Active-duty service members may keep valid home-state registration while stationed in Texas. If your registration was current, we present the proof and your orders to the prosecutor, and these tickets are usually dismissed.

faqs.q: Will I have to go to court?
faqs.a: Almost never. We file an appearance, gather your proof of registration and handle the pretrial docket for you. The only time you might appear is at a trial, which is rare for this type of ticket and something we would discuss with you first.

faqs.q: My registration ticket came with a no-insurance ticket. Can you handle both?
faqs.a: Yes. Multiple citations from the same stop are handled together, with each additional citation at a discounted add-on rate. See our no insurance ticket page for how we approach the insurance charge.
